hints: Recognize the shape of the graph: uniform acceleration from rest, followed by constant velocity $V$, followed by uniform deceleration to rest forms a trapezium.
Since the deceleration is twice the magnitude of the acceleration, the deceleration period takes half as long as the acceleration period: $20 / 2 = 10\text{ s}$.
Add the three time stages: $20\text{ s} + 170\text{ s} + 10\text{ s} = 200\text{ s}$ to find the total time.
walkthrough:
State the relationship between acceleration, deceleration, and the time taken to change velocity by $V$:
$$a = \frac{V}{t_{\text{acc}}} \quad \text{and} \quad d = \frac{V}{t_{\text{dec}}}$$
Since $d = 2a$, we have:
$$\frac{V}{t_{\text{dec}}} = 2\left(\frac{V}{t_{\text{acc}}}\right) \implies t_{\text{dec}} = \frac{t_{\text{acc}}}{2}$$

Compute the total time of motion across the three distinct phases:
$$t_{\text{total}} = t_{\text{acc}} + t_{\text{constant}} + t_{\text{dec}} = 20 + 170 + 10 = 200\text{ s}$$

Describe the key features of the sketch: the graph begins at the origin $(0, 0)$, rises linearly to $(20, V)$, remains constant at height $V$ until $t = 190\text{ s}$, and descends linearly to $(200, 0)$, with the descending line noticeably twice as steep as the ascending line.

hints: The total distance travelled is represented by the area under the velocity-time trapezium.
Convert the total distance from kilometres to metres: $2.775\text{ km} = 2775\text{ m}$.
walkthrough:
State the foundational physical principle: the area under a velocity-time graph represents the total distance travelled:
$$s = \text{Area under } v\text{-}t \text{ graph}$$

State the formula for the area of a trapezium:
$$\text{Area} = \frac{1}{2}(a + b)h$$
Here $a = 170\text{ s}$ is the duration of constant speed, $b = 200\text{ s}$ is the total duration, and $h = V$ is the maximum speed.

Convert distance into standard SI units:
$$s = 2.775\text{ km} = 2.775 \times 1000 = 2775\text{ m}$$

Substitute these values into the area equation:
$$\frac{1}{2}(170 + 200)V = 2775$$
$$\frac{1}{2}(370)V = 2775$$
$$185V = 2775$$
Divide both sides by $185$:
$$V = \frac{2775}{185} = 15\text{ m s}^{-1}$$

hints: The magnitude of acceleration is the gradient of the velocity-time graph during the first 20 seconds.
Use $a = \frac{V - u}{t}$ with $u = 0$, $V = 15\text{ m s}^{-1}$, and $t = 20\text{ s}$.
walkthrough:
State the definition of uniform acceleration as the rate of change of velocity:
$$a = \frac{v - u}{t}$$

Substitute the initial speed $u = 0\text{ m s}^{-1}$, the final speed of the acceleration phase $v = V = 15\text{ m s}^{-1}$, and the time taken $t = 20\text{ s}$:
$$a = \frac{15 - 0}{20} = \frac{15}{20}$$
